newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's fast-track privatisation nears end.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's fast-track privatisation nears end.

text.p: Hungary said on Tuesday it had raised three quarters of six billion forints expected from fast-track privatisations and would reach its target by the end of the year.
The process was launched last September to speed the sale of stakes in small and medium-sized companies by requiring bidders simply to offer more than a minimum price.
The APV privatisation agency would then sell the company to the highest bidder without considering other factors such as business plans.
APV's deputy managing director Imre Ragats told a news conference the six billion forint target was realistic.
"APV regards this method of privatisation as successful ...APV will be able to reach six billion forints of revenues," he said.
APV has offered stakes of between 25.8 to 100 percent in 121 companies with a total share capital of 22 billion forints and an average APV stake of 80 percent, APV said in a statement.

So far 72 companies have been sold, six of them to foreign investors, Ragats said, adding that the programme could be completed by the legal deadline of December 31, although the actual completion of some deals could spill over to 1997.
Most of the companies involved in the programme are part of the manufacturing and trade sectors, the statement said.
